youtube_video.title: Zoho vs Microsoft Dynamics 365: Which Suite Fits Your Business?
youtube_video.description:
Read the full comparison: https://zudoworks.com/insights/zoho-vs-microsoft-dynamics-365/

Zoho and Microsoft Dynamics 365 both sell a set of business applications that share one login and one set of customer data, but they package and license them in very different ways. Zoho One puts dozens of apps, including CRM, Books, Inventory, Desk, Projects, People, Creator and Analytics, under a single per-user licence, billed monthly or yearly. Dynamics 365 is a family of separate products: Sales, Customer Service, Field Service, Business Central, Finance and Supply Chain Management each have their own plans, and a person who needs two of them holds a base licence plus an attach licence. Every fact comes from Zoho's and Microsoft's own pages and Microsoft's Dynamics 365 Licensing Guide, read on 23 November 2026. We do not quote prices: check both vendors' pricing pages for your region.

Chapters
00:00 Zoho or Dynamics 365: not two CRM screens
00:06 Zoho One: one licence, dozens of apps

00:21 Where forecasting and custom records start
00:28 ERP: Business Central goes deeper
00:34 AI agents and credits
00:38 List people by role
00:43 Read the full comparison

Key facts from the comparison
- Zoho One lists an Essentials plan with 15+ apps and a Standard plan with 50+ apps on one licence per user.
- Zoho CRM has a free edition for 3 users and is billed monthly or yearly with no contract.
- In Dynamics 365, the first licence for a person must be the highest priced one (the base licence); further apps are attach licences.
- Forecasting and custom modules start at Zoho CRM Standard. On Microsoft's pricing page, forecasting and custom apps start at Sales Enterprise.
- Business Central Premium includes manufacturing. We did not find a production planning app in the Zoho One plan list.
- Sales Premium includes 1,000 Copilot Credits per user each month; Copilot Credits are required for Dynamics 365 agents.

The full guide also covers Zoho Creator vs Power Apps, Zoho Analytics vs Power BI, working with Outlook and Teams, a checklist before you sign with either, and a note for manufacturers.

Choosing between Zoho and Microsoft for a business of 10 to 250 people in the UK, US, Australia or New Zealand? Read the comparison and get in touch through zudoworks.com.

linkedin_profile_video:
When people ask me "Zoho or Dynamics 365?", they usually expect a CRM feature list.

I start somewhere else: who in your company sells, who invoices, who only approves, and who works in the warehouse.

Here's why. Zoho One gives each person dozens of apps on one licence. Dynamics 365 is bought product by product, with a base licence and attach licences per person, plus lighter Team Members licences for people who mostly read and approve.

A company where everyone needs CRM, accounts and helpdesk tends to find a bundle simpler. A company with 5 sellers and 40 people on the warehouse floor may land somewhere else.

And yes, we build on Zoho, so read me with that in mind. Where Microsoft is stronger, Business Central as a real ERP with manufacturing in Premium, I say so in the guide.

Two more things I'd check before signing either:

1. Which AI features sit inside the licence, and which draw on credits. On Microsoft's side, the Licensing Guide says Copilot Credits are required for any Dynamics 365 agents usage.
2. Storage. Dynamics 365 default capacity is per tenant and not cumulative, so a second product does not add a second allowance.

I put the comparison into 50 seconds. The written version is in the first comment.

One line on Microsoft's Dynamics 365 Sales pricing page changes most comparisons with Zoho CRM.

Forecasting, territory management and custom apps start at Sales Enterprise. On Zoho, forecasting and custom modules start at CRM Standard.

So comparing the entry plans on each page tells you very little. I always ask teams to write down the five features they cannot do without, then find the plan where each one begins.

The same goes for licensing. On Dynamics 365, name the base licence and each attach licence for every role. On Zoho One, decide between All Employee and Flexible User pricing, and ask what the renewal price will be, because on the day we checked the Standard All Employee price carried a "first year only" label.

Then run one real quote, one order and one invoice end to end in each trial. Zoho CRM has a free edition for 3 users, and Business Central has a 30-day trial, so there is no reason to decide from a demo alone.

I put the rest of the comparison into four slides: packaging, licensing, ERP depth and the numbers to check.

Full disclosure: we build on Zoho, so weigh my view with that in mind. Where Microsoft is the stronger choice, the guide says so plainly.
